about: workflow:find-and-classify-rows-by-rules: Keep the rows of one of the person's lists that match their rule tree (comparisons joined by all-of and any-of groups, each group optionally negated), evaluate a formula over the kept rows, and give e

payload.label: Find the rows of a list that match a person's rules, evaluate a formula over them, and label each row by the first rule that holds
payload.job: Keep the rows of one of the person's lists that match their rule tree (comparisons joined by all-of and any-of groups, each group optionally negated), evaluate a formula over the kept rows, and give each row the label of the first of the person's rules that holds. Logic has three states: a row whose value is unknown (missing or null) is kept only by a comparison that treats unknown as a value (is any of, is none of, is, is not, is known, is empty). A rule not finished is left out and named, never guessed.
payload.produces: The kept rows (their ids), the formula's value, each row's label, and the rules left out as incomplete, read from the store's own rows.

source.from: tools/formulas (do-work/requests.mjs, do-work/classify-by-rules.mjs, do-work/run-request.mjs, kits/*.json, tool-rows.json), read on trillion-workshop origin/main bb8022539c
source.note: The comparisons are the rule operators in tools/formula-engine/rules/rule-operators.json (the vocabulary the person picks from); the rule tree and the fields arrive in the request, so the recipe names no domain. Unknown in a comparison that must look at the value is no answer, and not-of-unknown stays unknown (a SQL NULL behaves the same way). A kept row needs a true answer. The rules that the workflow validator evaluates on admission stay in the shared evaluator (tools/formulas/do-work/requests.mjs), which other folders import; that library is not removed by this recipe.

list.description: The list whose rows are read

rules.description: The rule tree: {combinator: all-of|any-of, negate?, rules: [{field, op, value}] or nested groups}

formula.description: An optional formula over the kept rows, e.g. sum of one field

items.description: The label and its rule; the first label that holds names the row

steps.title: Read the list and what the store keeps
steps.do: Speak to the store in its own language, with the login under its credential_name, and read the list named in the request: its fields, their kinds, and where its rows are kept. Read tools/formula-engine/rules/rule-operators.json for the comparisons. Submit where the list's rows are kept (kept_in, or null) and the fields the rules name that the list has.

steps.title: Make no new objects; name what is missing
steps.do: The recipe makes no object of its own: it reads the list's rows and keeps nothing. A rule that names a field the list lacks is left out and named as incomplete. Submit the rules that can be evaluated and the ones left out.

steps.title: Prove the three-state rules on the example rows
steps.do: In a throwaway place in the same store, with example rows r1 (stage Negotiation, value 5000), r2 (stage Won, value null) and r3 (stage Lost, value 300): (1) rule value is more than 1000 keeps r1 only (r2 is unknown, so neither the comparison nor its negation holds it); (2) rule stage is none of [Lost] keeps r1 and r2; (3) rule value is not 300 keeps r1 and r2 (unknown equals nothing, so is not keeps it); (4) the formula sum of value over the rows of rule 2 is 5000; (5) labels: big when value is more than 1000, lost when stage is Lost, else other, so r1 big, r2 other, r3 lost. Submit each as kept ids, the formula value, or the labels.

steps.title: Answer the request
steps.do: Read the list's rows through the store's own query: keep a row only when the rule tree gives a true answer; a rule left out is named in incomplete and is not guessed; a row whose value has the wrong kind for a comparison is counted as an error row and left out. Evaluate the formula over the kept rows if one is named. Label each kept row by the first label whose rule holds, or leave it unlabelled. Submit kept (ids), value (the formula's answer or null), labels (row id to label), incomplete (rules left out) and error_rows (the count).

payload.erase: Nothing is kept by a read; labels are the person's own choice and are kept only when they say so.
